subject: Inference onramp: decision anchors, migration constraints and next steps
messages:
From: Grace O'Connor <grace.oconnor@redwood.inference>
To: Avi Kapoor <avi.kapoor@medalytics.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.inference>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.inference>
Date: Sat, 18 Apr 2026 10:12:00 -0700
Subject: Inference onramp: decision anchors, migration constraints and next steps

Hi Avi / Nora —

Thanks for taking the time today — good conversation. Quick recap + proposed next steps so we keep momentum while your infra/ procurement teams align.

Recap (what I captured)
- Current state: in-house GPU cluster (NVIDIA A100), mix of inference and training workload, latency-sensitive customer-facing features.
- Primary constraints: EU data residency, SOC 2 evidence required, procurement window ~6–8 weeks.
- Shortlist options you asked about: Redwood Hosted API (fastest to ship POC), Redwood Dedicated (reserved GPU pool for predictable throughput), Private (VPC/on-prem package for full isolation).
- Migration sources: you mentioned migrating from an internal API fronting the legacy cluster and a small set of experiments on a public LLM API.

Key decision anchors we need to confirm
1) POC acceptance criteria — latency (p95) target, cost per 1k requests, and sample prompt set to run.
2) Data residency + retention policy details (EU region + retention duration).
3) Expected steady-state throughput (rps/tps) and KV cache reuse patterns (are requests highly repetitive?).

Attachments: if you can share the infra diagram and the short requirements spreadsheet you referenced, that’ll speed sizing.

Proposed next steps
- You: share two items (infra diagram PDF, current-reqs-summary.xlsx) — target EOD Tue, Apr 20.
- Us: solutions deep-dive — we’ll propose a short matrix (Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private) highlighting tradeoffs and a rough cost/latency estimate.
- Schedule: 45m technical deep-dive w/ infra and security — are you available Wed Apr 21 10:00–11:00 CET or Thu Apr 22 14:00–15:00 CET?

I’ve looped Ben (solutions) and Karthik (security/compliance) so we can respond quickly on SOC2/controls questions. Thanks again — short bullets here to keep things actionable.

Best,
Grace O'Connor
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
grace.oconnor@redwood.inference
(415) 555-0176

P.S. Reference: HubSpot deal DL-8342 (linked), I’ll attach the POC checklist and a short decision matrix after we get your diagram.

From: Avi Kapoor <avi.kapoor@medalytics.com>
To: Grace O'Connor <grace.oconnor@redwood.inference>
Cc: Nora Feldman <nora.feldman@medalytics.com>
Date: Sat, 18 Apr 2026 15:04:00 +0100
Subject: Re: Inference onramp: decision anchors, migration constraints and next steps

Thanks Grace — helpful summary. Quick responses inline: 

- Infra diagram + short reqs: attaching now (medalytics_infra_diagram_v1.pdf, current-reqs-summary.xlsx). The cluster is co-located in our Frankfurt DC; we currently run two 8-GPU A100 boxes behind an internal inferencing API.
- Throughput: baseline 8–12 rps during peak; expected growth to ~30 rps in 6 months during feature ramp.
- Latency target: p95 < 300ms for standard prompts; can accept slightly higher for long-form generation.
- KV reuse: moderate for identical prompts from the UI but low reuse for ad-hoc analyst queries.
- Data residency: all customer data must remain in EU, logs retained for 90 days.
- SOC 2: we have a vendor checklist; we’ll need SOC2 Type II evidence or equivalent plus answers on logging/audit retention.
- Procurement: finance needs an SOW and pricing outline — 6–8 week procurement. POC ideally before procurement commit.

We’re open to starting with Hosted for a narrow POC (EU-only region) if it means faster validation, but long-term preference is Dedicated or Private depending on cost and control.

Available for the technical deep-dive: Wed Apr 21 10:00 CET works for me.

—Avi
Avi Kapoor
Head of Platform Engineering | Medalytics
avi.kapoor@medalytics.com
+44 20 7946 0958

Attachment: medalytics_infra_diagram_v1.pdf (diagram), current-reqs-summary.xlsx (xlsx)

From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.inference>
To: Avi Kapoor <avi.kapoor@medalytics.com>, Nora Feldman <nora.feldman@medalytics.com>
Cc: Grace O'Connor <grace.oconnor@redwood.inference>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.inference>
Date: Mon, 20 Apr 2026 08:17:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Inference onramp: decision anchors, migration constraints and next steps

Avi / Nora — thanks for the diagram and numbers, that’s exactly what we need. High-level takeaways from a solutions perspective: 

- Hosted (fastest POC): We can spin an EU-region Hosted tenant and route only selected traffic. Pros: days to validate, minimal ops. Cons: data residency controls and SOC2 evidence are questions we’ll need to scope (we have SOC2 for our platform; we can provide relevant artifacts).

- Dedicated (recommended mid-term): Reserved GPU pool in your EU region. Predictable performance for 30+ rps and easier isolation for audit controls. We'll provide sizing options: 1x8xA100 equiv for initial Dedicated pool with autoscale headroom.

- Private (on-prem/VPC): Full isolation; good for strict compliance but higher ops and longer lead time (interviews, hardware validation, network configuration).

Sizing and cost quick note (very rough):
- POC Hosted: demo tenant + 2 realtime vCPU nodes — minimal cost; expected to validate latency profile in 24–72h.
- Dedicated starter: 1 reserved 8xA100 equivalent (target), monthly reserved pricing estimate attached in the POC pack we’ll send.

Questions we still need from you before the deep-dive:
1) Any absolute blackout for Hosted (e.g., legal reasons)?
2) Are there any firewall/peering constraints for Private options (can your network team accept peering from a Redwood-managed VPC)?
3) Do you have an internal SSO provider (SAML/Okta) we should integrate for the POC?

Next steps: we’ll prepare a 2‑slide decision matrix + rough cost bands and an initial SOW-lite for procurement prep. I’ll send those by EOD Mon Apr 20 (CET). Confirming: Wed Apr 21 10:00 CET for the technical deep-dive — I’ll invite the solutions + security folks and include a short agenda.

Thanks,
Ben Carter
Solutions Engineering | Redwood Inference
ben.carter@redwood.inference

On security/compliance: looping Karthik to start collecting the SOC2 artifacts and to surface any blockers ahead of the deep-dive.

From: Nora Feldman <nora.feldman@medalytics.com>
To: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.inference>, Grace O'Connor <grace.oconnor@redwood.inference>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.inference>, Avi Kapoor <avi.kapoor@medalytics.com>
Date: Tue, 20 Apr 2026 09:03:00 +0100
Subject: Re: Inference onramp: decision anchors, migration constraints and next steps

Thanks Ben — that plan works. A couple quick notes before Wednesday:
- No absolute legal block on Hosted for a limited POC as long as EU-only tenancy and logs stay in-region.
- Network: we can accept VPC peering for Private but need the security team to sign off — I’ll have our network lead on the call.
- SSO: we use Okta (SAML).

We’ll be ready with a couple of prompt examples for the POC and can share procurement timelines on the call. See you Wed 21 Apr 10:00 CET.

-Nora
Nora Feldman
Director of Security & Compliance | Medalytics
nora.feldman@medalytics.com
